subproblem.title: Normalisation of the Euclidean coefficient norm: Σ_j α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|_E² for every orthonormal basis f
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P (a continuous alternating n-linear form, Covector (Euclid P) n) and let f = (f_0, …, f_{P−1}) be an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P. Then Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f_{j(0)}, …, f_{j(n−1)})² = n!·|α|_E², where |α|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} and e is the standard basis.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n) (f : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ (Euclid P)), ∑ j : Fin n → Fin P, (α (fun k => f (j k))) ^ 2 = (n.factorial : ℝ) * covectorEuclideanNorm α ^ 2
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1(i)–(ii) of the parent node's supplied proof of the mass formula M_W(T) = R.measure W (Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3), chapter-06.txt lines 763–766; coefficient norm of (6.1.5)/(6.1.15)). Notation (shared with the parent proof): ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with standard orthonormal basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i; Λ^n = Covector (Euclid P) n, the continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P; for a family b : Fin P → ℝ^P and j : Fin n → Fin P write b∘j := (b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(n−1)}); |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} [I strictly increasing] α(e∘I)²) (SimonGMT Chapter06/Mass.lean). For a family b put S_b(α) := Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(b∘j)². We must show S_f(α) = n!·|α|_E².

1. (Square of the norm.) The radicand Σ_I [I strictly increasing] α(e∘I)² is a finite sum of nonnegative terms, so |α|_E² = Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e∘I)² (Real.sq_sqrt).

2. (Basis independence by slotwise Parseval.) Let b, b' be orthonormal bases of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P. For m = 0, 1, …, n put H_m := Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(w_m(j))², where w_m(j)(k) := b_{j(k)} if k < m and w_m(j)(k) := b'_{j(k)} if k ≥ m. Then H_0 = S_{b'}(α) and H_n = S_b(α). Fix m < n and split every j into its m-th value i := j(m) ∈ Fin P and its values j' on the other n − 1 slots (j ↦ (j(m), j') is a bijection, e.g. via Fin.insertNth / Fin.removeNth). For fixed j' the map λ_{j'}(v) := α(u_0, …, u_{m−1}, v, u_{m+1}, …, u_{n−1}), with u_k := b_{j(k)} for k < m and u_k := b'_{j(k)} for k > m, is a linear functional of v ∈ ℝ^P (α is multilinear). Writing λ_{j'}(v) = ⟨r, v⟩ with r := Σ_a λ_{j'}(e_a) e_a, Parseval for orthonormal bases (OrthonormalBasis.sum_sq_inner_right) gives Σ_i λ_{j'}(b_i)² = ‖r‖² = Σ_i λ_{j'}(b'_i)². The terms of H_{m+1} with fixed j' are exactly the λ_{j'}(b_i)² (i ∈ Fin P) and those of H_m are the λ_{j'}(b'_i)²; summing over j' gives H_{m+1} = H_m. By induction on m, S_b(α) = S_{b'}(α); in particular S_f(α) = S_e(α). (Equivalent implementation: expand b_i = Σ_a ⟨e_a, b_i⟩ e_a in every slot by multilinearity and use Σ_i ⟨e_a, b_i⟩⟨e_{a'}, b_i⟩ = δ_{aa'} (OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner) in each of the n slots; all cross terms cancel and S_b(α) = S_e(α).)

3. (Non-injective tuples.) If j is not injective then e∘j is not injective (e is injective), so α(e∘j) = 0 because α is alternating (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_not_injective). Hence S_e(α) = Σ_{j injective} α(e∘j)².

4. (Injective tuples = increasing tuples × permutations.) Every injective j : Fin n → Fin P factors uniquely as j = I∘π with I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing and π ∈ Perm(Fin n). Existence: with σ := Tuple.sort j, j∘σ is monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort) and injective, hence strictly increasing; take I := j∘σ and π := σ⁻¹. Uniqueness: if I∘π = I'∘π' with I, I' strictly increasing, then I and I' have the same range, and a strictly increasing map Fin n → Fin P is determined by its range (it is the increasing enumeration of that n-element set, cf. StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT / Finset.orderEmbOfFin_unique), so I = I'; then π = π' because I is injective. Conversely each such I∘π is injective. Thus (I, π) ↦ I∘π is a bijection from {I strictly increasing} × Perm(Fin n) onto {j injective}.

5. (Signs.) For I strictly increasing and π ∈ Perm(Fin n), α(e∘I∘π) = sign(π)·α(e∘I) (AlternatingMap.map_perm applied to α.toAlternatingMap), so α(e∘(I∘π))² = α(e∘I)².

6. (Counting.) By steps 3–5, S_e(α) = Σ_{I strictly increasing} Σ_{π ∈ Perm(Fin n)} α(e∘I)² = |Perm(Fin n)|·Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e∘I)² = n!·|α|_E² (Fintype.card_perm, Fintype.card_fin and step 1).

7. (Conclusion.) By steps 2 and 6, Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f∘j)² = S_f(α) = S_e(α) = n!·|α|_E². The same argument covers n = 0 (one empty tuple, which is strictly increasing; 0! = 1) and n > P (no injective and no strictly increasing tuples; both sides are 0). ∎
proof_key_steps: |α|_E² equals the sum of α(e∘I)² over strictly increasing I.
Slotwise Parseval (hybrid sums H_m) shows Σ_j α(b∘j)² is the same for every orthonormal basis b.
Non-injective tuples contribute 0; injective tuples are exactly I∘π (I increasing, π a permutation) and contribute α(e∘I)² each.
Counting the n! permutations gives Σ_j α(e∘j)² = n!·|α|_E², hence Σ_j α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|_E².

audit.reason: The proposition matches the prose and coefficient-norm definition. Slotwise Parseval proves basis independence; sorting injective tuples and counting permutations gives the factorial normalization. The argument also covers n = 0 and n > P without additional hypotheses.

subproblem.title: Measurable selection of a near-maximizing unit covector field
subproblem.statement: Let μ be a measure on ℝ^P, ξ : ℝ^P → MultiVector P n be μ-a.e. strongly measurable, η > 0, and assume that for μ-a.e. x there is an n-covector β with |β|_E ≤ 1 and ξ(x)(β) = 1. Then there is a strongly measurable g : ℝ^P → Covector (Euclid P) n with |g(x)|_E ≤ 1 for every x and 1 − η ≤ ξ(x)(g(x)) for μ-a.e. x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n) (η : ℝ), 0 < η → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∃ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm β ≤ 1 ∧ ξ x β = 1) → ∃ g : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n, StronglyMeasurable g ∧ (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (g x) ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 1 - η ≤ ξ x (g x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3.1 of the parent node's supplied proof of the mass formula M_W(T) = R.measure W (countable dense subset of B_E and the disjointified sets A_k), stated for a general measure and without the cutoff to K (the cutoff to K is applied by the caller). Notation (shared with the parent proof): ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with standard orthonormal basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i; Λ^n = Covector (Euclid P) n, the continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P; for a family b : Fin P → ℝ^P and j : Fin n → Fin P write b∘j := (b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(n−1)}); |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} [I strictly increasing] α(e∘I)²) (SimonGMT Chapter06/Mass.lean).

1. (Λ^n is finite dimensional and separable.) The linear map ev : Λ^n → ((Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ), α ↦ (j ↦ α(e∘j)) is injective: if all α(e∘j) vanish, the multilinear map underlying α vanishes on all tuples of basis vectors and hence is 0 (Module.Basis.ext_alternating, or Module.Basis.ext_multilinear with the standard basis in every slot). By Module.Finite.of_injective, Λ^n is finite dimensional over ℝ (Mathlib has no global instance FiniteDimensional ℝ (Covector (Euclid P) n); establish it locally). A finite-dimensional real normed space is proper (FiniteDimensional.proper_real), hence second countable and separable.

2. (Countable dense subset of the unit ball.) |·|_E is continuous on Λ^n (square root of a finite sum of squares of the continuous linear functionals α ↦ α(e∘I)), so B := {β : |β|_E ≤ 1} is closed; it is nonempty since |0|_E = 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero). As a subset of a separable metric space, B is separable (TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.mono), so there is a countable D ⊆ B with B ⊆ closure D (TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.exists_countable_dense_subset). D is nonempty (0 ∈ B ⊆ closure D); enumerate D = {β_k : k ∈ ℕ} (Set.Countable.exists_eq_range).

3. (Strongly measurable version.) Let ξ̃ := (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk) be strongly measurable with ξ = ξ̃ μ-a.e. For each k, x ↦ ξ̃(x)(β_k) is strongly measurable (evaluation at β_k is a continuous linear map on MultiVector P n), so A_k := {x : 1 − η < ξ̃(x)(β_k)} is a measurable set.

4. (Selection.) Put A'_k := A_k ∖ ⋃_{i<k} A_i (pairwise disjoint measurable sets with ⋃_k A'_k = ⋃_k A_k) and define g(x) := β_k if x ∈ A'_k, g(x) := 0 if x ∉ ⋃_k A_k. Then g(x) ∈ D ∪ {0} ⊆ B, so |g(x)|_E ≤ 1 for all x. g is strongly measurable: it is the pointwise limit of the simple functions g_N := Σ_{k<N} A'_k.indicator (fun _ ↦ β_k) (for each x the sequence g_N(x) is eventually constant, equal to g(x)); use stronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto (or define g with Nat.find on the measurable predicate and prove strong measurability piecewise).

5. (Near-maximality.) For μ-a.e. x we have ξ(x) = ξ̃(x) and some β ∈ B with ξ(x)(β) = 1. The set {β' ∈ Λ^n : 1 − η < ξ(x)(β')} is open (ξ(x) is continuous) and contains β ∈ B ⊆ closure D, so it contains some β_k; thus x ∈ A_k ⊆ ⋃_i A_i. Let k' be the least index with x ∈ A_{k'}; then x ∈ A'_{k'}, g(x) = β_{k'} and ξ(x)(g(x)) = ξ̃(x)(β_{k'}) > 1 − η. Hence 1 − η ≤ ξ(x)(g(x)) for μ-a.e. x. ∎
proof_key_steps: Λ^n is finite dimensional (injective coefficient map), hence separable; the closed unit ball B of |·|_E has a countable dense subset {β_k}.
Replace ξ by a strongly measurable version ξ̃; the sets A_k = {1 − η < ξ̃(x)(β_k)} are measurable.
g := β_k on A'_k = A_k ∖ ⋃_{i<k} A_i (0 elsewhere) is strongly measurable with |g|_E ≤ 1.
By density and continuity of ξ(x), a.e. x lies in some A_k, so ξ(x)(g(x)) > 1 − η a.e.

audit.reason: The injective coefficient map establishes finite dimensionality and separability. A strongly measurable version of ξ and a countable dense subset of the coefficient unit ball give measurable disjoint selection sets. Their simple-function approximations produce the required everywhere bounded strongly measurable field, with the stated almost-everywhere estimate.

subproblem.title: Evaluation on an orthonormal n-frame is bounded by the Euclidean coefficient norm: |α(τ)| ≤ |α|_E
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) n) and let τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P. Then |α(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1})| ≤ |α|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm α.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → |α τ| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1(a) of the parent node's supplied proof of the mass formula M_W(T) = R.measure W (Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3)). Notation (shared with the parent proof): ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with standard orthonormal basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i; Λ^n = Covector (Euclid P) n, the continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P; for a family b : Fin P → ℝ^P and j : Fin n → Fin P write b∘j := (b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(n−1)}); |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} [I strictly increasing] α(e∘I)²) (SimonGMT Chapter06/Mass.lean). Uses the sibling lemma regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis: for every orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P, Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|_E².

1. (n ≤ P and an orthonormal basis extending τ.) τ is orthonormal, hence linearly independent, so n = card(Fin n) ≤ finrank ℝ ℝ^P = P (Orthonormal.linearIndependent, LinearIndependent.fintype_card_le_finrank, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). subproblem.title: A unit covector attaining 1 on an orthonormal frame: |β_τ|_E = 1 and β_τ(τ) = 1
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P. Then there is an n-covector β on ℝ^P with |β|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm β = 1 and β(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) = 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → ∃ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm β = 1 ∧ β τ = 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1(b) of the parent node's supplied proof of the mass formula M_W(T) = R.measure W (Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3); the determinant formula (6.1.1) for wedges). Notation (shared with the parent proof): ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with standard orthonormal basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i; Λ^n = Covector (Euclid P) n, the continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P; for a family b : Fin P → ℝ^P and j : Fin n → Fin P write b∘j := (b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(n−1)}); |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} [I strictly increasing] α(e∘I)²) (SimonGMT Chapter06/Mass.lean). Uses the sibling lemma regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis: Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|_E² for every orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P. Implementation note: wedgeCovectors and wedgeCovectors_apply_det live in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.FormsDuality, which is not in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission; import it (and Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Permutation if Matrix.det_permutation is used) in the implementation's helper module.

1. (Definition of β.) Let β := wedgeCovectors n (fun i ↦ innerSL ℝ (τ i)) ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n, the wedge of the 1-covectors ⟨τ_i, ·⟩. By SimonGMT Chapter06.wedgeCovectors_apply_det, for every v : Fin n → ℝ^P, β(v) = det M(v) with M(v) := Matrix.of (fun i k ↦ ⟨τ_i, v_k⟩).

2. (β(τ) = 1.) By orthonormality ⟨τ_i, τ_k⟩ = (if i = k then 1 else 0) (orthonormal_iff_ite), so M(τ) = 1 and β(τ) = det 1 = 1.

3. (n ≤ P and an orthonormal basis extending τ.) τ is orthonormal, hence linearly independent, so n = card(Fin n) ≤ finrank ℝ ℝ^P = P (Orthonormal.linearIndependent, LinearIndependent.fintype_card_le_finrank, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). Let ι : Fin n → Fin P, ι(k) := Fin.castLE (n ≤ P) k (injective). Define v : Fin P → ℝ^P by v(i) := τ(⟨i, h⟩) if h : i.val < n and v(i) := 0 otherwise, and s := {i : Fin P | i.val < n}. The restriction of v to s is τ composed with the bijection s ≃ Fin n, hence orthonormal. Since finrank ℝ ℝ^P = P = card(Fin P), Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq gives an orthonormal basis f : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ ℝ^P with f(i) = v(i) for all i ∈ s; in particular f(ι(k)) = τ(k) for every k ∈ Fin n.

4. (Values on basis tuples.) Fix j : Fin n → Fin P and put M := M(f∘j). Since f is orthonormal and τ_i = f_{ι(i)}, M_{ik} = ⟨f_{ι(i)}, f_{j(k)}⟩ = (if ι(i) = j(k) then 1 else 0).
 (a) If j = ι∘π for some π ∈ Perm(Fin n), then f∘j = (f∘ι)∘π = τ∘π, so β(f∘j) = β(τ∘π) = sign(π)·β(τ) = sign(π) = ±1 (AlternatingMap.map_perm applied to β.toAlternatingMap, and step 2); hence β(f∘j)² = 1. (Equivalently, M is a permutation matrix and Matrix.det_permutation applies.)
 (b) Otherwise β(f∘j) = 0. If some j(k) ∉ range ι, column k of M is zero and det M = 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_column_eq_zero). If range j ⊆ range ι, then j = ι∘ρ where ρ(k) is the unique preimage of j(k) under ι; ρ : Fin n → Fin n is not a permutation (else we are in case (a)), so ρ is not injective (an injective self-map of a finite type is bijective, Finite.injective_iff_bijective); then j and f∘j are not injective and β(f∘j) = 0 because β is alternating (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_not_injective).
 (c) π ↦ ι∘π is injective, so exactly n! = |Perm(Fin n)| tuples fall under (a). Hence Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} β(f∘j)² = n!.

5. (Norm.) By regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis applied to P, n, β, f: n! = n!·|β|_E². As n! > 0, |β|_E² = 1, and as |β|_E ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg), |β|_E = 1.

6. (Conclusion.) By steps 2 and 5, covectorEuclideanNorm β = 1 and β τ = 1. ∎

For an orthonormal basis f extending τ, β(f∘j) = ±1 when j = ι∘π for a permutation π and 0 otherwise, so Σ_j β(f∘j)² = n!.
The sibling identity gives n! = n!·|β|_E², hence |β|_E = 1.

subproblem.title: Smooth admissible approximation in L¹ of a finite measure (density of C_c, cutoff, radial retraction, mollification)
subproblem.statement: Let ν be a finite measure on ℝ^P, O ⊆ ℝ^P open, K ⊆ O compact and g : ℝ^P → Covector (Euclid P) n ν-a.e. strongly measurable with |g(x)|_E ≤ 1 for all x and g(x) = 0 for all x ∉ K. Then for every ε > 0 there is a smooth compactly supported n-form h (IsTestForm h) with tsupport h ⊆ O, |h(z)|_E ≤ 1 for all z, and ∫⁻ ofReal(|h(x) − g(x)|_E) dν(x) < ofReal(ε).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (O K : Set (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n), IsFiniteMeasure ν → IsOpen O → IsCompact K → K ⊆ O → AEStronglyMeasurable g ν → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (g x) ≤ 1) → (∀ x, x ∉ K → g x = 0) → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ h : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, IsTestForm h ∧ tsupport h ⊆ O ∧ (∀ z, covectorEuclideanNorm (h z) ≤ 1) ∧ ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (covectorEuclideanNorm (h x - g x)) ∂ν < ENNReal.ofReal ε
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0 and 3.2 of the parent node's supplied proof of the mass formula M_W(T) = R.measure W (there ν = μ⌞O). Notation (shared with the parent proof): ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with standard orthonormal basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i; Λ^n = Covector (Euclid P) n, the continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P; for a family b : Fin P → ℝ^P and j : Fin n → Fin P write b∘j := (b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(n−1)}); |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} [I strictly increasing] α(e∘I)²) (SimonGMT Chapter06/Mass.lean). Uses the sibling lemma regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le (|α(τ)| ≤ |α|_E for orthonormal τ). ‖·‖ denotes the operator norm of Λ^n (its Mathlib norm); IsTestForm h means ContDiff ℝ ∞ h ∧ HasCompactSupport h. Implementation note: the C_c-density and bump-convolution lemmas cited below need Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ContinuousMapDense and Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.Convolution (and Mathlib.Geometry.Manifold.SmoothApprox for the optional remark), which are not in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission; import them in the implementation's helper module.

0. (The coefficient norm.) Let N := Fin n → Fin P and define Φ : Λ^n → EuclideanSpace ℝ N by Φ(α)_j := α(e∘j) if j is strictly increasing and 0 otherwise. Φ is linear, and each coordinate is a continuous linear functional (|α(e∘j)| ≤ ‖α‖·Π_k ‖e_{j(k)}‖ = ‖α‖), so Φ is a continuous linear map; by EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, |α|_E = ‖Φ(α)‖. Consequently:
 (a) |·|_E is a continuous seminorm: |α + β|_E ≤ |α|_E + |β|_E, |cα|_E = |c|·|α|_E, |α − β|_E = |β − α|_E.
 (b) |α|_E ≤ c₁‖α‖ with c₁ := 1 + ‖Φ‖ ≥ 1.
 (c) ‖α‖ ≤ c₂|α|_E with c₂ := P^n: for v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) expand v_k = Σ_i (v_k)_i e_i; multilinearity gives α(v) = Σ_{j ∈ N} (Π_k (v_k)_{j(k)})·α(e∘j) (ContinuousMultilinearMap.map_sum); if j is injective, (e_{j(0)}, …, e_{j(n−1)}) is orthonormal and |α(e∘j)| ≤ |α|_E by regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le; if j is not injective, α(e∘j) = 0 (alternating). As |(v_k)_i| ≤ ‖v_k‖, |α(v)| ≤ P^n·|α|_E·Π_k ‖v_k‖, so ‖α‖ ≤ P^n|α|_E (ContinuousMultilinearMap.opNorm_le_bound).
 (d) (Radial retraction.) For v ∈ Λ^n put π(v) := (max 1 |v|_E)⁻¹ • v. Then π is continuous, π(0) = 0, |π(v)|_E ≤ 1, π(v) = v if |v|_E ≤ 1, and |π(v) − b|_E ≤ |v − b|_E whenever |b|_E ≤ 1. For the last claim assume s := |v|_E > 1 and put x := Φ(v), y := Φ(b) in the inner product space EuclideanSpace ℝ N, so ‖x‖ = s, ‖y‖ ≤ 1 and Φ(π(v)) = x/s. Then ‖x − y‖² − ‖x/s − y‖² = s² − 1 − 2(1 − 1/s)⟨x, y⟩ ≥ s² − 1 − 2(1 − 1/s)s = (s − 1)² ≥ 0, using ⟨x, y⟩ ≤ ‖x‖‖y‖ ≤ s and 1 − 1/s > 0.

1. (Integrability and continuous approximation.) Put V := (ν ℝ^P).toReal (ν is finite). By 0(c), ‖g(x)‖ ≤ c₂ for all x; with g ν-a.e. strongly measurable and ν finite, g is ν-integrable (Integrable.of_bound / integrable_of_bounded). ν is a finite Borel measure on the σ-compact metric space ℝ^P, hence regular (instance Measure.Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure). By Integrable.exists_hasCompactSupport_lintegral_sub_le (Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ContinuousMapDense) there is a continuous, compactly supported g₀ : ℝ^P → Λ^n with ∫⁻ ‖g(x) − g₀(x)‖ₑ dν ≤ ofReal(ε/(4c₁)). By 0(b), ofReal|g₀(x) − g(x)|_E ≤ c₁‖g(x) − g₀(x)‖ₑ, so ∫⁻ ofReal|g₀ − g|_E dν ≤ ofReal(ε/4).

2. (Cutoff.) By exists_compact_between choose a compact L with K ⊆ interior L and L ⊆ O. By Urysohn's lemma (exists_continuous_one_zero_of_isCompact for K and the closed set (interior L)ᶜ) there is a continuous χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with χ = 1 on K and χ = 0 off interior L; hence tsupport χ ⊆ L. Put g₁ := χ • g₀: continuous with tsupport g₁ ⊆ L. Since g = 0 off K and χ = 1 on K, g = χ • g, so g₁ − g = χ • (g₀ − g) and |g₁(x) − g(x)|_E = χ(x)|g₀(x) − g(x)|_E ≤ |g₀(x) − g(x)|_E (0(a)). Therefore ∫⁻ ofReal|g₁ − g|_E dν ≤ ofReal(ε/4).

3. (Retraction.) Put g₂ := π ∘ g₁. It is continuous, vanishes wherever g₁ does (π(0) = 0), so tsupport g₂ ⊆ L, and |g₂(x)|_E ≤ 1. By 0(d) with b := g(x) (|g(x)|_E ≤ 1), |g₂(x) − g(x)|_E ≤ |g₁(x) − g(x)|_E, so ∫⁻ ofReal|g₂ − g|_E dν ≤ ofReal(ε/4).

4. (Mollification.) g₂ is continuous with compact support, hence uniformly continuous (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous). Let κ := ε/(4c₁(1 + V)) > 0. Choose r₀ > 0 with cthickening r₀ L ⊆ O (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open) and r₁ > 0 with ‖g₂(x) − g₂(y)‖ ≤ κ whenever dist(x, y) < r₁. Let φ : ContDiffBump (0 : ℝ^P) have φ.rOut < min r₀ r₁, let φ_n := φ.normed volume (smooth, ≥ 0, ∫ φ_n = 1, support φ_n = ball(0, φ.rOut)) and h := φ_n ⋆[lsmul ℝ ℝ, volume] g₂, i.e. h(z) = ∫ φ_n(t)·g₂(z − t) dt.
 (a) h is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left with ℕ∞-order ⊤; g₂ is locally integrable) and has compact support (HasCompactSupport.convolution), so IsTestForm h.
 (b) support h ⊆ support φ_n + support g₂ ⊆ ball(0, φ.rOut) + L ⊆ cthickening r₀ L (support_convolution_subset); cthickening r₀ L is closed, so tsupport h ⊆ cthickening r₀ L ⊆ O.
 (c) |h(z)|_E ≤ 1: Φ(h(z)) = ∫ φ_n(t)·Φ(g₂(z − t)) dt (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm; the integrand is continuous with compact support), so |h(z)|_E = ‖Φ(h(z))‖ ≤ ∫ φ_n(t)·‖Φ(g₂(z − t))‖ dt ≤ ∫ φ_n = 1 (norm_integral_le_integral_norm, φ_n ≥ 0, |g₂|_E ≤ 1).
 (d) For every z, g₂ varies by at most κ on ball(z, φ.rOut) (φ.rOut < r₁), so ‖h(z) − g₂(z)‖ ≤ κ (ContDiffBump.dist_normed_convolution_le) and |h(z) − g₂(z)|_E ≤ c₁κ by 0(b).

subproblem.title: Upper mass bound for an integer multiplicity current: M_W(τ(M, θ, ξ)) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n and R = (C, θ, ξ) an IMRep in U with R.Represents T (T(ω) = ∫_C θ ξ(ω) dHⁿ for all test forms ω in U). Then for every set W ⊆ ℝ^P, M_W(T) = T.massOn W ≤ R.measure W = (θ Hⁿ⌞C)(W).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), T.massOn W ≤ R.measure W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent node's supplied proof of the mass formula M_W(T) = R.measure W (Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3); mass (6.2.5)). Notation: C := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, μ_C := μHE[n].restrict C, so R.action ω = ∫ θ ξ(ω) dμ_C and R.measure = μ_C.withDensity θ; |·|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm. Uses the sibling lemma regcomp_unit_orientation_pairing (part (i)). Openness of U or W is not needed.

1. (Reduction.) T.massOn W = sSup {ofReal(T ω) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W}, where ω is admissible iff ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(z)|_E ≤ 1 for all z. By sSup_le it suffices to prove ofReal(T ω) ≤ R.measure W for each admissible ω.

2. (Setup.) Fix an admissible ω and put S := tsupport ω; S is closed, hence a Borel set, and S ⊆ W.

3. (Pointwise bound.) By R.orients, for μ_C-a.e. x there is Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q, so by regcomp_unit_orientation_pairing (i), |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α|_E for all α. For such x: if x ∈ S then |θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ θ(x)·|ω(x)|_E ≤ θ(x); if x ∉ S then ω(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and θ(x)·ξ(x)(0) = 0. Hence ‖θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x))‖ₑ ≤ S.indicator θ (x) (in [0, ∞]) for μ_C-a.e. x.

4. (Integral estimate.) By R.Represents T, T ω = R.action ω = ∫ θ ξ(ω) dμ_C. Then ofReal(T ω) ≤ ofReal|T ω| = ‖T ω‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻ ‖θ ξ(ω)‖ₑ dμ_C (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm, valid without any integrability hypothesis) ≤ ∫⁻ S.indicator θ dμ_C (lintegral_mono_ae and step 3) = ∫⁻_S θ dμ_C (lintegral_indicator, S measurable) = (μ_C.withDensity θ)(S) = R.measure S (withDensity_apply, S measurable) ≤ R.measure W (measure_mono, S ⊆ W).

5. (Conclusion.) Taking the supremum over admissible ω, T.massOn W ≤ R.measure W. ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to ofReal(T ω) ≤ R.measure W for each admissible ω.
A.e. on C, ‖θ ξ(ω)‖ₑ ≤ θ·1_{tsupport ω} by the unit orientation pairing and |ω|_E ≤ 1.
ofReal(T ω) ≤ ∫⁻ ‖θ ξ(ω)‖ₑ dHⁿ⌞C ≤ R.measure(tsupport ω) ≤ R.measure W.

subproblem.title: Lower mass bound for an integer multiplicity current: ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ ≤ M_W(τ(M, θ, ξ)) for open W
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n and R = (C, θ, ξ) an IMRep in U with R.Represents T. Then for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, R.measure W = (θ Hⁿ⌞C)(W) ≤ M_W(T) = T.massOn W.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → R.measure W ≤ T.massOn W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0 and 3 of the parent node's supplied proof of the mass formula M_W(T) = R.measure W (Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3)). Notation: C := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, μ_C := μHE[n].restrict C, μ := R.measure = μ_C.withDensity θ, |·|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm. Sibling lemmas used: regcomp_unit_orientation_pairing ((i) |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α|_E, (ii) ∃ β, |β|_E ≤ 1 ∧ ξ(x)(β) = 1, whenever IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q), regcomp_covector_field_near_maximizer and regcomp_exists_smooth_unit_form_approx (statements as frozen).

1. (Consequences of the orientation condition.) By R.orients and regcomp_unit_orientation_pairing, for μ_C-a.e. x: (i) |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α|_E for all α, and (ii) there is β with |β|_E ≤ 1 and ξ(x)(β) = 1.

2. (Reduction to W' := W ∩ U.) W' is open. μ(Uᶜ) = 0: μ ≪ μ_C (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous) and μ_C(Uᶜ) = μHE[n](Uᶜ ∩ C) = 0 since C ⊆ U (R.carrier_subset). Hence μ(W) ≤ μ(W') + μ(Uᶜ) = μ(W') (measure_mono, measure_union_le). It therefore suffices to show c ≤ T.massOn W for every c ∈ ℝ≥0∞ with c < μ(W') (then μ(W') ≤ T.massOn W by le_of_forall_lt).

3. (Compact exhaustion.) Fix c < μ(W'). There are compact sets K_0 ⊆ K_1 ⊆ ⋯ with ⋃_j K_j = W': if W' = ℝ^P take K_j := closedBall(0, j); otherwise let d(z) := infDist z W'ᶜ (continuous, and d(z) > 0 iff z ∈ W' because W'ᶜ is closed and nonempty: IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos) and take K_j := closedBall(0, j) ∩ {z : 1/(j + 1) ≤ d(z)} (closed and bounded, hence compact in the proper space ℝ^P; contained in W'; increasing; every z ∈ W' lies in K_j for j large). [Equivalently: IsOpen.exists_iUnion_isClosed gives closed F_j increasing to W'; take K_j := F_j ∩ closedBall(0, j).] By continuity of μ from below (tendsto_measure_iUnion_atTop), μ(K_j) → μ(W'), so there is a compact K ⊆ W' with c < μ(K).

4. (Open neighbourhood with finite measure.) By exists_compact_between choose a compact L with K ⊆ interior L and L ⊆ W'; put O := interior L. Then O is open and K ⊆ O ⊆ L ⊆ W' ⊆ W ∩ U. Moreover μ(L) = ∫⁻_L θ dμ_C = ∫⁻_{C ∩ L} θ dμHE[n] < ∞ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, and R.locallyIntegrable_mult for the compact set L ⊆ U). Hence μ(K) ≤ μ(O) ≤ μ(L) < ∞ and ν := μ.restrict O is a finite measure. Put m := μ(K).toReal, so μ(K) = ofReal m and c < ofReal m.

5. (Fix η ∈ (0, 1): near-maximizing field.) By 1(ii) and R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient, regcomp_covector_field_near_maximizer applied to μ_C, ξ and η yields a strongly measurable g₀ with |g₀(x)|_E ≤ 1 for all x and 1 − η ≤ ξ(x)(g₀(x)) for μ_C-a.e. x. Put g := K.indicator g₀: strongly measurable (K is closed, StronglyMeasurable.indicator), |g(x)|_E ≤ 1 for all x (|0|_E = 0), and g(x) = 0 for x ∉ K.

6. (Lower bound for the model integral.) Let F(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(g(x)). F is μ_C-a.e. strongly measurable (θ measurable; x ↦ ξ(x)(g(x)) is the continuous evaluation map applied to the a.e. strongly measurable pair (ξ, g)), and by 1(i) |F| ≤ θ·1_K μ_C-a.e.; since ∫⁻ θ·1_K dμ_C = μ(K) < ∞, F is μ_C-integrable. μ_C-a.e. F ≥ (1 − η)·θ·1_K (on K by step 5, off K both sides vanish).
